      "texture": "Only the hero title block gets texture: a faint 1 px grout grid in grout sand at 30 percent behind the square Kufic word, like glazed bricks set between plain ones. All other surfaces stay flat limestone paper.",
      "imagery": "One square Kufic panel per screen, drawn on an 8 by 8 or 12 by 12 module and carrying a real, readable, non-sacred word the user approved, such as the product name or a section name like اهلا or المجلس. Use turquoise strokes on limestone, or brick strokes with grout lines between them. Photos are tight square crops of plain brick and tile walls with no inscriptions shown.",
      "motion": {

Steal: the square module, the right-angle turns, the even stroke and gap width and the glazed-brick-against-plain-brick color logic, applied only to words the user chooses. Credit: credit the brick and tile makers of Iran and Central Asia who built banna'i square Kufic, alongside the wider Arabic calligraphic tradition and its calligraphers. Care: care tier, so this card takes the construction grammar and not the sacred content: never set Quran verses, names of God or the shahada as decoration, never use invented letters as pattern, and keep every Kufic word real, readable, approved by the user and off anything disposable or tappable."
